issues.legal_issue: A building-purpose lease for an indefinite period after an initial fixed term, construed as a whole, may create a permanent tenancy rather than a tenancy at will or a tenancy limited to the lessee’s lifetime.
material_facts: The lease was for agricultural land to be used for a factory and other buildings, and it authorized the lessee to erect and alter substantial structures.
The lease set an initial twenty-year term, after which the lessee could continue in possession for as long as desired by paying the stipulated rent.
The lessor agreed not to require the lessee to give up possession while the lessee wished to retain the land and observed the lease terms.
The lease was expressed to bind the parties’ heirs, successors, and assigns, and the lessee could sublet or re-let the land.
The lessee could surrender the lease after the initial term, but the lessor had no corresponding right to terminate it at will.
The lower courts decreed ejectment, and the High Court treated the post-term tenancy as one for an indefinite period rather than a permanent tenancy.
issues.conclusion: The lease created a permanent tenancy, so the ejectment decree was set aside and the suit was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The nature of a tenancy must be determined by construing the lease as a whole and identifying the parties’ intention. A lease of land for building purposes without a fixed period raises a presumption of a permanent tenancy; the presumption is supported where the lease is heritable and assignable and the lessor has no right to terminate possession. The lessee’s right to surrender does not by itself rebut that presumption. The Court applied the principles in Navalram v. Javerilal, Promada Nath Roy v. Srigobind Chowdhry, Forbes v. Hanuman Bhagat, Commissioner of Income-tax v. Maharajadhiraj Kumar Visheshwar Singh, Janaki Nath Roy v. Dina Nath Kundu, and Baboo Lekhraj Roy v. Kunhya Singh, and distinguished Babasaheb v. West Patent Co., Ltd. No statutory provision was relied on.

rule.if: appeal_against_ejectment_decree and building_purpose_lease and indefinite_continuation_after_initial_term and lessor_cannot_end_possession_at_will and lease_binds_successors and lease_allows_assignment

predicates.appeal_against_ejectment_decree: The proceeding is an appeal from a decree ordering the lessee or a successor to surrender possession.
predicates.building_purpose_lease: The land was leased for building purposes, and the lease authorized the construction of substantial buildings or structures.
predicates.indefinite_continuation_after_initial_te: After an initial fixed term, the lessee could continue in possession for as long as desired under the lease terms.
predicates.lessor_cannot_end_possession_at_will: The lessor agreed not to require the lessee to give up possession while the lessee wished to remain and complied with the lease.
predicates.lease_binds_successors: The lease states that its terms bind the parties’ heirs or successors.
predicates.lease_allows_assignment: The lease permits the lessee to transfer the leasehold interest or sublet the land.

issues.definition: When an ejectment appeal concerns a building-purpose lease that continues indefinitely after an initial term, bars the lessor from ending possession at will, binds successors, and allows assignment, the rule treats the tenancy as permanent.

issues.legal_issue: A lessee’s right to surrender a lease, when not matched by a lessor’s right to terminate it, is compatible with a permanent tenancy, including where the parties agreed in advance to permit surrender.
material_facts: The lease gave the lessee liberty to surrender after the initial term and end the obligation to pay future rent.
The lease did not give the lessor a corresponding right to require the lessee to surrender possession.
The lease was for building purposes and otherwise contained terms indicating an intention to create a permanent, heritable, and assignable tenancy.
issues.conclusion: The lessee’s surrender right did not derogate from the permanent nature of the tenancy.
issues.legal_principle: A lessee may surrender a leasehold interest to the lessor by mutual consent, and the parties need not wait until the time of surrender to agree to it; they may stipulate for surrender in advance. A surrender option reserved for the lessee’s benefit does not contradict a permanent tenancy when the lessor has no corresponding termination right. The Court relied on its construction of the lease as a whole and the principles in Janaki Nath Roy v. Dina Nath Kundu and Baboo Lekhraj Roy v. Kunhya Singh; it distinguished Babasaheb v. West Patent Co., Ltd. No statutory provision was relied on.

rule.if: appeal_concerning_lease_tenancy and lessee_may_surrender and lessor_lacks_matching_termination_right and lease_otherwise_indicates_permanency

predicates.appeal_concerning_lease_tenancy: The proceeding concerns whether the terms of a lease create a permanent tenancy.
predicates.lessee_may_surrender: The lease allows the lessee to surrender the leasehold and end future rent obligations.
predicates.lessor_lacks_matching_termination_right: The lease does not allow the lessor to require surrender merely at the lessor’s choice.
predicates.lease_otherwise_indicates_permanency: The lease’s other terms indicate a permanent tenancy, including its building purpose or its binding effect on successors.

issues.definition: Where a lease permits the lessee to surrender, gives the lessor no matching termination right, and otherwise indicates a permanent tenancy, the surrender option is compatible with that tenancy.
